newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast crude prices inch up amid idle trade.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast crude prices inch up amid idle trade.

text.p: Prices for U.S. West Coast light crude oil inched up Thursday, following West Texas Intermediate (WTI) in an otherwise listless spot market, traders said.

The discount for West Coast Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude -- the regional benchmark -- remained at $2.16 under August spot prices WTI. Buyers said they stayed out of the market to figure out schedules for shipping August crude.
Arco Pipeline Co plans to announce its apportionment Monday for Line 63, the major pipeline between California's San Joaquin Valley (SJV) oil fields and Los Angeles refineries.
Key seller BP continued to offer ANS at $1.85 under August WTI, but heard no bids.
Outright prices for ANS crude rose to $17.45/17.60 a barrel, six cents over Wednesday.
Meanwhile, Kern River grade remained 10 to 20 cents over postings.
Wilmington crude, pumped from Long Beach, Calif., stood 65 to 75 cents over posting, unchanged for over a month.
Light grade Line 63 crude remained unchanged at $3.05 under WTI and about $1.00 over Buena Vista crude.
